maria: Heads-up: saw a perf regression on KV-prefetch path when we switched kernel selector. Trying an nsys capture to prove it's kernel-choice + batching interaction.
cheng: good call. do a bracketed capture around the failing request pattern so we don't blow up file size.
sam: what's your exact nsys CLI? i always forget the right sampling + osrt combo.
maria: i used this locally and it gave a clean timeline:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o kv-prefetch-test.qdrep \\n  --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=bracket_start \\n  --capture-range-end=bracket_end --sample=cpu:1ms --duration=20s \\n  --sample-clock=cpu
```
maria: notes: 1) bracket the section with NVTX markers in the runtime (bracket_start/ brack_end) so we only capture the steady failure window, 2) use osrt to get kernel scheduling and stream timings, 3) 1ms cpu sample rate is small but helps find cpu-side batching stalls.
cheng: +1. Also warm up model for 2-3 iterations before bracket_start (KV cache warm paths change after first few requests). otherwise traces show cold-path kernels and confuse the selector analysis.
sam: when you open the qdrep in the GUI, what timeline panes do you check first?
maria: kernel timeline -> filter by CU occupancy and duration, then stream view to see overlapping memcpy/kernels. look for repeated short <1ms kernels that might be getting coalesced wrong by selector.
maria: I also diff two runs (old selector vs new selector) and export a CSV of kernel durations from the timeline to quickly plot regressions. small script:
```python
# pseudocode to extract durations from qdrep (using nsys-export or UI export)
# iterate rows where event.type == 'Kernel' and collect name and duration_us
```
cheng: FYI, if file size still huge, switch sampling to 5ms and increase bracket precision. sampling bias can hide microsecond hotspots so validate with a short full-trace (no sampling) on one smaller run.
perf-bot: Deploy-check: perf/regression KVPREF-43 attached qdrep: s3://redwood-perf/1748897654/kv-prefetch-test.qdrep :thumbsup:
maria: final reminder — annotate NVTX with batch size + KV hit ratio to correlate kernel mix with batching heuristics. small metadata in markers saves so much manual correlation later.
sam: awesome, can you drop the qdrep link in the regression ticket and tag me? I'll run the selector experiment with forced affinity.
maria: done, link is in KVPREF-43. thanks all.
